# Tag input: `jl-tag-input`

A field that collects short texts as removable chips.

- Class `JlTagInput`, a molecule: `import { JlTagInput } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/tag-input

A field that collects short texts as chips: topics, labels, skills, email addresses. Enter or a comma
adds what was typed, and so does leaving the field; Enter in the empty field submits the form, as from a native
field. Backspace in the empty field takes the last chip back, and a
pasted list ("design, research, writing" or one per line) adds each of its items. The same tag twice, whatever its
case, is not added: the chip already there flashes instead.

From the field, Left (at the start of the text) reaches the chips' remove buttons; Left and Right move between
them, Backspace or Delete removes one. With suggestions, a short list offers the matching ones while people type.
In a form, each tag is its own entry under the field's name, like checkboxes sharing a name.

## Use

```ts
import { JlTagInput } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlTagInput
  label="Skills"
  placeholder="Add a skill"
  suggestions={["Accessibility","Animation","Back end","Data visualisation","Design systems","DevOps","Front end","Illustration","Research","Security","Testing","Typography","Writing"]}
  value={["Design systems","Front end"]}
/>
```

```html
<jl-tag-input
  label="Skills"
  placeholder="Add a skill"
  suggestions='["Accessibility","Animation","Back end","Data visualisation","Design systems","DevOps","Front end","Illustration","Research","Security","Testing","Typography","Writing"]'
  value='["Design systems","Front end"]'
></jl-tag-input>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `value` (attribute `value`): `string[]`, default `[]`. The tags, in order.
- `placeholder` (attribute `placeholder`): `string`, default `''`. Shown while there is no tag.
- `suggestions` (attribute `suggestions`): `string[]`, default `[]`. Tags offered in a list while people type.
- `max` (attribute `max`): `number`, default `0`. The most tags it takes; 0 for no limit.
- `size` (attribute `size`): `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`, default `'md'`. The height of a line of chips.
- `name` (attribute `name`): `string`, default `''`. The field's name in the form's data: each tag is an entry under it.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The accessible name, when no visible label names the field.
- `required` (attribute `required`): `boolean`, default `false`. The form cannot be submitted without a tag.
- `disabled` (attribute `disabled`): `boolean`, default `false`. The chips show, but nothing can be added or removed.
- `invalid` (attribute `invalid`): `boolean`, default `false`. Drawn in the danger colour, for an error the page found.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `change` (`onChange` in JSX), detail `string[]`: A tag was added or removed.

## Methods

- `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`: Focuses the text field.
- `checkValidity(): boolean`: Whether a required field has a tag.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The frame around the chips and the text field.
- `list` (part, `::part(list)`): The floating list of suggestions.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### Typing and pasting

Type a word and press Enter or a comma, or paste a list.

```html
<div class="narrow">
  <jl-tag-input label="Topics" placeholder="Add a topic" value='["web components","design tokens"]'></jl-tag-input>
</div>
```

### Suggestions

Type "de": the matching suggestions show; the arrows and Enter, or a click, take one.

```html
<div class="narrow">
  <jl-tag-input label="Skills" placeholder="Add a skill" suggestions='["Accessibility","Animation","Back end","Data visualisation","Design systems","DevOps","Front end","Illustration","Research","Security","Testing","Typography","Writing"]'></jl-tag-input>
</div>
```

### A maximum

Three labels at most: past that, what is typed stays in the field.

```html
<div class="narrow">
  <jl-tag-input label="Labels" max="3" value='["bug","needs review"]' placeholder="Up to three labels"></jl-tag-input>
</div>
```

### In a form

The form gets each tag under the name "to", as several fields of one name.

```html
<form class="stack narrow demo-invite">
  <jl-tag-input name="to" label="Invite" placeholder="Email addresses" required value='["ada@example.com"]'></jl-tag-input>
  <div class="row">
    <jl-button type="submit" variant="primary" label="Send invitations"></jl-button>
  </div>
  <p class="muted demo-invite-out">Submit to see the form data.</p>
</form>
```

```js
const form = root.querySelector('.demo-invite');
const out = root.querySelector('.demo-invite-out');
form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  out.textContent = `to = ${JSON.stringify(new FormData(form).getAll('to'))}`;
});
```

### Sizes, states and listening

The paragraph listens to change.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-tag-input class="demo-count" label="Keywords" placeholder="Add keywords" size="sm"></jl-tag-input>
  <jl-tag-input label="Large" size="lg" value='["large"]'></jl-tag-input>
  <jl-tag-input label="Disabled" disabled value='["locked","read only"]'></jl-tag-input>
  <p class="muted demo-count-out">No keyword yet.</p>
</div>
```

```js
const input = root.querySelector('.demo-count');
const out = root.querySelector('.demo-count-out');
input.events.register('change', (tags) => {
  out.textContent = `${tags.length} keyword(s): ${tags.join(', ')}`;
});
```
